title_prefix: The 'connection dead' warning is a reap
mechanism: handle-peer-fin (src/networking/ibd.lisp:1591-1609, driven from drain-and-reap-peer at :1872) consults exactly one thing -- (not (connection-connected conn)) -- and then logs 'Peer ~A connection dead - disconnecting' at WARN and disconnects. No clock, no counter, no peer state, no reason. Seven distinct sites write that flag: a send-queue flush error (src/networking/connection.lisp:454), two send-bytes error paths (:532, :540), %abandon-receive for EOF/IO-error/partial-consumption give-up (:645), and the v2 transport's oversize packet, failed body read and Poly1305 auth failure (src/networking/v2-transport.lisp:167, :182, :191). Five of the seven log nothing of their own, so for those this line is the only record; the two v2 ones emit their own WARN first, so those disconnects print two lines. Our own liveness verdicts -- check-peer-health, connection-receive-expired-p, retry-timed-out-requests, consider-peer-eviction -- each log a distinct line and call disconnect-peer directly, and disconnect-peer sets peer-connection to NIL (src/networking/peer.lisp:458-463), so a peer they judged can never reach handle-peer-fin: 100% of this line's occurrences are socket-level reaps, never a liveness judgement. Core separates the two and logs the reap at LogDebug(BCLog::NET) with the reason on the line: 'socket closed, disconnecting peer=%d' for recv()==0 and 'socket recv error, disconnecting peer=%d: %s' (refs/bitcoin/src/net.cpp:2196-2215 at d3056bc), and InactivityCheck's own reasons -- 'socket no message in first %i seconds', 'socket sending timeout: %is', 'socket receive timeout: %is', 'V2 handshake timeout', 'version handshake timeout' (:2008-2059) -- all through CNode::DisconnectMsg (:709-713).
consequence: Ordinary peer turnover is reported as a fault. Our log-warn is unconditional at the default level (src/logging.lisp:325-336), while every Core line this corresponds to is LogDebug(BCLog::NET) and therefore silent unless the operator asks for -debug=net (src/logging.lisp:386, :467-470 is our equivalent gate, which this line does not use): a node whose remote peers close N sockets an hour prints N WARN lines where Core prints zero at default verbosity. The line is also unactionable as logged -- it cannot distinguish a peer that hung up from a v2 authentication failure from our own send error -- and, because it is emitted for a peer in ANY state, it says nothing about whether the peer was healthy. The live observation the finding cites (50-70 lines an hour on the testnet4/mainnet nodes) is inherited, not re-observed here; what I can state from the tree is that all of it is socket-level churn and none of it is a liveness verdict, and that Core's counterpart for the same events is off by default. Cosmetic/observability only -- no behaviour change, the reap itself is correct and mirrors SocketHandlerConnected -- so S3.
evidence: Container /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-misc-s3b, warm image, probe build/ga11probe/fin.lisp, reading the emitted entries out of bl.log:*log-buffer*. Three different causes and two peer states produce the byte-identical line: (:CAUSE :EOF-ABANDON-RECEIVE :STATE-BEFORE :READY :REAPED T :STATE-AFTER :DISCONNECTED :LOG-LINES ('[...] [warning] Peer 203.0.113.7 connection dead - disconnecting')), the same for :SEND-ERROR on a :READY peer and for a v2 auth failure on a :HANDSHAKING peer; a peer whose connection is still up gives (:REAPED NIL :STATE-AFTER :READY :LOG-LINES NIL), which is the negative control. The [warning] tag in the captured entry is the level. Ours: src/networking/ibd.lisp:1591-1609, :1860-1872; src/networking/connection.lisp:454, :532, :540, :645; src/networking/v2-transport.lisp:167, :182, :191; src/networking/peer.lisp:458-463; src/logging.lisp:325-336, :386, :455-470. Core: net.cpp:709-713 (DisconnectMsg), :2196-2215 (SocketHandlerConnected), :2008-2059 (InactivityCheck).
fix_shape: Attach the reason and lower the level to Core's. Give the connection a disconnect-reason slot that each of the seven writers sets as it clears connection-connected (:peer-closed for the EOF path, :recv-error, :send-error, :v2-oversize-packet, :v2-body-read-failed, :v2-auth-failure), then have handle-peer-fin report it through (bl:log-cat "net" ...) in Core's shape -- reason first, then 'disconnecting peer=<id>' -- so the line is silent unless -debug=net is on, exactly like LogDebug(BCLog::NET), and carries the same information CNode::DisconnectMsg does. The two v2 sites that already log their own WARN should drop to the same category line rather than printing twice. Leave the reap behaviour itself alone: it is Core-faithful and the finding is about what is logged, not what is done. A test should assert that each writer's reason survives to the line and that the line is absent at the default log level and present with the net category enabled, both directions, so the gate cannot pass vacuously.
